newsitem.title: USA: CME live cattle seen steady to off, feeders steady.
newsitem.headline: CME live cattle seen steady to off, feeders steady.

text.p: CME live cattle futures were expected to open steady to 0.150 cent per lb lower while feeder cattle were called steady, livestock analysts said.

Toppy wholesale boxed beef prices and expected lower packer bids for fed cattle were expected to encourage selling. Beef demand is expected to slip seasonally as summer unfolds and temperatures rise and packers have more contract cattle available in July than they had in June, analysts said.
The USDA Cold Storage report on Friday could be slightly constructive for beef but it may have more effect on boneless beef contracts than on live cattle contracts, sources noted.
The report showed frozen beef stocks down nearly 5.0 million lbs during the month.

Feeder cattle futures were seen mostly steady after closing higher on Friday. Although the latest CME feeder cattle index slipped slightly, it was still at highest levels in nearly three years. Expectations of lower corn futures Monday and declining feed costs into the fall were also seen as supportive and may offset pressure from slow fed cattle markets, they said.
The latest CME feeder cattle index was off $0.02 at $78.01 per cwt.
